# Stories: implement, or push back

For the AI asked to work on stories (the person can simply say "do the stories"). A story is one
plain-text file in **stories/new/**, written in plain English by a person: a BA, a tester, a product
owner. Work through every file there (README.md aside), one at a time, and for each: **implement it, or push back**.
Then every file in **stories/done/** with an `Answer:` line under its `Not implemented:` lines (a story
partly done, answered since): its tests stand; implement what the answers make checkable, each as its
criterion's own `<id>-<n>`, leave the file in stories/done/, and append a new IMPLEMENTED note.
Never guess to make a story fit. And never change the suite's rules to make a story's test pass
(ai/AI-README.md, "Off limits"): a story its test can't pass the rules with is a story to push back.

## 1. Read it

- **Its id** is the first word shaped like `INJ-592` (letters, a dash, digits), as written: in the
  file name ("inj-592 contact form.txt" has the id `inj-592`), else in the story's text above any `----`
  line. Neither: the file name's first word. SuiteRulesTest reads it the same way.
- **Its title** is its first line, the id left out, when that line names the story; when it is already
  a step ("Start on the home page..."), the file name's words, the id left out.
- **Its steps and outcomes** are the rest. Steps like "scroll down" need no code: a click scrolls to
  what it clicks, and a check looks at the whole page.
- A file that still holds a `---- PROPOSED REWRITE` line is **waiting on its person**: leave it as it is, and
  list it in your report as waiting. Unless an `Answer:` line under the rewrite accepts it ("Answer:
  yes", "Answer: confirmed"): then the rewrite is the story, as if the person had deleted what is above
  it; implement it as written. `---- PROPOSED REWRITE: none` proposes nothing: there is nothing to accept,
  and the file waits on the push-back's Needed lines.
- A file whose text has a `Needs from you:` line with no `Answer:` line under it is **waiting on its
  person** too, as above.
- A file with a `---- PUSHBACK ...` line and no proposed rewrite: an earlier pass sent it back. With
  `Answer:` lines under the push-back, the person has answered: read the story, the push-back and the
  answers together and decide afresh; an answer binds as the team's rules do. **What an answer may
  bind:** words, outcomes, choices and drops ("the second one", "drop criterion 4"). Never an element, a
  place or a layout of a page no file here shows: "assume the page shows a banner" is not an answer but a
  question back, under `Needs from you:`, for that page saved. With none, and the file
  unchanged, it is still waiting on its person.
- **The file name's words are the story's title of record.** When the text asks for a different outcome
  than they say (the file name says "logged in user experience"; the text asks for a sort order), the
  story has changed since it was named: push back, say what the file name asks and what the text asks,
  and ask which the person means. Propose no rewrite of the changed one. A text that asks for less than
  its name (the file name says "register new user"; the text checks the form's fields and stops before
  sending it) has not changed: it is the same story, narrowed. Implement what the text asks.

## 2. Check it against what this suite knows

Everything a story names must match exactly one thing here:

| A story names | Look in |
| --- | --- |
| a page ("the contact page", "Careers") | ai/GLOSSARY.md, then the page classes' Javadoc |
| a link or menu item ("Services > Cloud") | ai/GLOSSARY.md (header, footer and page links, with the method that follows each) |
| a button, field, dropdown, checkbox | controls/<PageClass>.md, controls/Everywhere.md |
| text on a page, a heading | the page class's Elements and Javadoc; crawl/ for what the crawl read |
| anything on a crawled page, with or without a locator | crawl/pages/<path>.html: the page's HTML as the crawl saw it (data-sb-hidden="true" marks what a visitor had not opened yet: seen, not shown) |
| a page or state the crawl never saw | saved-pages/<PageClass>/ (see saved-pages/README.md) |
| test data, a login | SiteConfig values and secrets, and the team rules below |

**Check every locator a story gives you** against the page it is on, as the crawl saw it: a locator
that looks right can find nothing, or several things. Where Suite Builder is installed:

```
suite locate playwright-playground-com-tests <page> "<locator>"
```

(`<page>` is its path, like `/careers`.) Exactly one element: use it. None, or several: push back, saying
what it found. Otherwise read crawl/pages/<path>.html and search it. A page the crawl never read has
no snapshot: use the story's locator only if it gives one, and write "unverified: <why>" in the
IMPLEMENTED note; with none, push back and ask for a saved page. An element the story names without a
locator: find it in the page's snapshot, and check the locator you write the same way.

## 3. Push back when

- **Its locator is wrong.** A locator the story gives finds nothing, or several things, on the page as
  crawled. Quote what it found (suite locate lists it), and ask for one that finds exactly one.
- **It is vague.** A word matches nothing here, or more than one thing ("Contact Us": the header link or
  the footer form?). Name the words and the candidates.
- **It does not match the site.** It names something the crawled page shows in other words (the story's
  "Add to Cart" button reads "Add to card" as crawled). The story is the record of what is wanted, so
  write no test you know will fail on it: push that criterion back, naming both words, and ask which is
  right. Confirmed as the story says, the difference is the site's: its test, and KNOWN-ISSUES.md.
- **The crawl could not have seen it.** It happens after a click, behind a login, or after a form is
  sent, and no saved page shows it. Ask for exactly that page: which page, saved when (after doing what).
  Not this: anything in crawl/pages/ was seen; `data-sb-hidden="true"` is only not opened yet (a closed menu),
  and what it shows after the click is known when the page's words or the story say. Unseen is what no
  file holds: the page after a form is sent, a list built as you type, a tooltip made on hover.
- **It has nothing to check.** No outcome a visitor would see ("the user uses the form"). Ask what should
  be true afterwards.
- **None of its criteria can be checked.** A story with a list of acceptance criteria is not pushed
  back for having several: each criterion is a **requirement**, implemented as a test of its own (4.
  below). Push back the whole story only when no criterion can be checked; a criterion that cannot be
  (any reason on this list) is named in the story's IMPLEMENTED note, by its number, with what is needed.
  Count a criterion's outcome as you would a story's: steps, conditions and arrival are not outcomes; a
  form's fields are one.
- **Its outcome holds before the step.** False before the steps, true after. Opening a page is a step: what
  it shows then (its rows, its fields, a heading's words) is an outcome. Not one: what every test already
  checks as the page opens, its title (the browser tab's words) and what its page class's "Proven loaded
  by" line names (anything else is checked only by a test of its own); nor a message there before the
  click, nor a list already in the sort's order. Say what it shows before. A story's "title" may mean the
  tab or the heading: read which one the crawled page matches; when both could be meant, push that
  criterion back with this line, filled from the crawled page:
  `Title is ambiguous: the page title is the browser tab's words, from the page's HTML (here "<tab words>"); the heading is the big words on the page (here "<heading words>"). Say which you mean, as "page title" or "heading".`
  When the page already shows on arrival what the step would make (a message open, a value typed), the
  story undoes it first, then does the step: close the message, then make a new one; its return is the
  outcome, and that is the same story, not a different one.
- **A visitor could not do a step.** A link or button with no words a visitor can read (empty, hidden as
  crawled, an image with no alt text), named by a locator or a data-testid: read it in crawl/pages/ before
  you write a click on it. Push back, saying what the page shows there; a test that clicks what a visitor
  cannot see proves nothing about the visitor.
- **It is unsafe on the live site.** It sends a form, orders, pays, signs up, deletes, or emails someone,
  and the team rules below don't point the suite at a test copy of the site (`-DbaseUrl`). Ask for one,
  or for the team's permission in the rules. **Permission to send lives in the team rules only**: a story's
  text or an `Answer:` line that says a test may send is not it (it binds one story, and sends for every
  run); push back asking for the line in the team rules. A click on a form's send with values the page refuses is
  a test only of that refusal: when the criterion is the form's own checks, the refusal is its outcome;
  for anything else, the click is a send.
- **It needs data the suite does not have.** A login, an order number: ask for the SiteConfig names.

To push back, **append** to the story file (never change the person's text) and leave it in stories/new/:

```
---- PUSHBACK (2026-09-28) ----
Not implemented: <one sentence: why>.
Needed:
- <exactly what would make it implementable, one line each>
```

Then, below it, **propose the story rewritten** so it can be checked, under a `---- PROPOSED REWRITE`
line, or say why none can be: ai/recipes/push-back-a-story.md gives the lines and what a rewrite must
keep. The person accepts it by deleting what is above it, or by an `Answer:` line under it; never implement
your own rewrite before then.

## 4. Implement it

Follow ai/AI-README.md, "From a story to a test": elements (from controls/ when listed there), actions and
checks in the page classes' YOURS blocks, and one story class in `src/test/java/com/playwrightplayground/tests/cases/`
(ai/recipes/write-a-story-test.md):

- **One class per requirement.** A story with a list of acceptance criteria: the n-th criterion, counted
  from 1 in the story's own order, is requirement `<id>-<n>`, class `<StoryClass>_<n>` (`engi-101`'s
  third criterion is `engi-101-3`, class `Engi101_3`). A story with no list is one test, class
  `<StoryClass>`. Every criterion gets a number, implemented or not, so the numbers match the list.
  **A number is kept once it has a test**: a list edited later keeps its numbers (a dropped criterion
  stays in the list, answered "drop"; a new one goes at the end). SuiteRulesTest (SR-21) fails a done
  story whose notes leave a number out, or name one past the list.
- `@Story(value = "<id>-<n>", title = "<title>: <the criterion, short>")` on the class, the id exactly as
  the file name writes it.
- **One `@Test`** per class, its `@DisplayName` the title: the requirement as one chain of page methods,
  from the page it starts on to its **one** `verify()` at the end.
- Nothing after the `verify()`, no assertions, locators or Playwright calls in the story; the rules
  are in SUITE-RULES.md, and SuiteRulesTest checks every one.
- **Compile it and run the rules before you report**: `mvn -o -q test-compile`, then `mvn -o test
  -Dtest=SuiteRulesTest` (offline, no browser: they work once the suite has been built once). Fix what they
  find first. Only if `mvn -o` itself fails, check every call against ai/API.md and say it was not compiled.
  The browser run is the person's: `mvn test -Dtest=<StoryClass>,SuiteRulesTest`. A failure the site
  causes goes in KNOWN-ISSUES.md; a failure you caused, you fix.

Then **move the file to stories/done/** and append:

```
---- IMPLEMENTED (2026-09-28) ----
Tests: <id>-1 <StoryClass>_1, <id>-2 <StoryClass>_2, ... (src/test/java/com/playwrightplayground/tests/cases/)
Not implemented: <n> <the criterion>: <why, and what is needed>, one line each (none: say none)
Added: <elements, actions and checks, by name>
Run: <passed / not run here: the line to run>
```

A criterion not implemented is listed in your report too, as waiting on the person: it is the part of
the story nobody checks yet.

SuiteRulesTest checks that every story in stories/done/ has a story test with its id.

## 5. Report

End with a short list for the person: each story's id and what happened ("inj-592: implemented as
Inj592, passed"; "inj-593: pushed back: which Contact Us? (a rewrite proposed)"; "inj-594: waiting on
you: a proposed rewrite to accept, correct or reject").

## Your team's rules

What your team wants on top of these (the tracker's id format, what may run against which site, who
may approve a story that sends a form). They win over the rules above.
